key_insight: A guided diffusion model can reconstruct physically realistic bubbly-flow velocity fields from phase-limited 2D measurements, including the difficult bubble phase.
engineering_relevance: This offers a generative-prior approach for recovering inaccessible flow regions in multiphase experiments and could reduce measurement gaps in turbulent flow diagnostics.
method: Train on 2D slices extracted from fully resolved 3D DNS of buoyancy-driven bubbly flows.
Generate velocity fields unconditionally or conditioned on surrounding liquid-phase flow.
Use a simple slice-patching procedure to extend reconstruction toward 3D bubble interiors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that reconstructed bubble-phase fields accurately reproduce key statistical features and that adjacent-slice patching yields a reasonable 3D reconstruction inside a bubble.
watch_item: The 3D result relies on simple patching of 2D slices, so continuity and accuracy may degrade away from the trained slice distribution or in more complex multiphase regimes.
paper_title: Gappy Reconstruction of Bubbly Flows by Guided Diffusion Models
